```typescript
const updated: Task = {

  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

This code explicitly assigns every field from `updates`, even when those fields are `undefined`. In JavaScript, spreading `{ ...existing, title: undefined }` results in `title` being `undefined`, effectively erasing the existing value.

The fix uses conditional spreads - only spreading a field if it's actually defined in the updates:

```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  ...(updates.priority !== undefined && { priority: updates.priority }),
  ...(updates.status !== undefined && { status: updates.status }),
  ...(updates.dueDate !== undefined && { dueDate: updates.dueDate }),
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

Now if `updates.title` is undefined, the title is not included in the spread, so it keeps the existing value from `existing`.

## Summary

The bug was in `src/task-manager.ts` in the `updateTask` method. The original code was:

```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

This code explicitly assigns every field from `updates`, even when those fields are `undefined`. In JavaScript, spreading `{ ...existing, title: undefined }` results in `title` being `undefined`, effectively erasing the existing value.

The fix uses conditional spreads - only spreading a field if it's actually defined in the updates:

```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  ...(updates.priority !== undefined && { priority: updates.priority }),
  ...(updates.status !== undefined && { status: updates.status }),
  ...(updates.dueDate !== undefined && { dueDate: updates.dueDate }),
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

Now if `updates.title` is undefined, the title is not included in the spread, so it keeps the existing value from `existing`.

## Summary of the Fix

The bug was in `src/task-manager.ts` in the `updateTask` method. The original code explicitly assigned every field from `updates` regardless of whether it was defined:

```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,        // overwrites with undefined if missing!
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  ...
};
```

In JavaScript, `{ ...existing, title: undefined }` sets `title` to `undefined`, erasing the existing value.

**The fix** uses conditional spreads so only fields that are actually defined in the update are merged in:

```typescript
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  ...(updates.title !== undefined && { title: updates.title.trim() }),
  ...(updates.description !== undefined && { description: updates.description }),
  ...(updates.priority !== undefined && { priority: updates.priority }),
  ...(updates.status !== undefined && { status: updates.status }),
  ...(updates.dueDate !== undefined && { dueDate: updates.dueDate }),
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

If `updates.title` is `undefined`, the spread is skipped, so the existing value from `existing` is preserved. The `title` is also trimmed (consistent with `createTask`). All 11 tests pass.
